Anna (Docs): I opened a small PR to add an "edge routing" example to the capacity handbook. It shows fallback to a lower-cost model and a routing snippet for cost-tiered traffic. Also renamed the SDK param from `tenant_hint` -> `tenant_label` in the examples. Can folks sanity-check anchors, wording for SLAs, and the SDK snippet? PR: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 :eyes:

Ravi (Eng-Platform): Thanks — paste the minimal YAML and the SDK example here and I can run the linkcheck + a quick local build. Also call out any anchor changes you made so I can search for broken refs.

Anna (Docs): YAML snippet (for routing policy):
```yaml
routing:
  prioritize: [cost-tier, latency]
  fallbacks:
    - model: rdm-small-v1
      when: capacity_constrained
      reason: "lower-cost fallback to maintain SLO"
```
SDK example (JS):
```js
await client.createRoute({
  model: 'rdm-large-v1',
  tenant_label: 'acct-42', // renamed from tenant_hint
  routing: { policy: 'cost-first' }
});
```

Maya (Eng-ML): For the param rename: please add a short migration note. A tiny snippet showing the mapping helps customers: `tenant_label = tenant_hint || tenant_label` (or explicit migration utility). Also ensure we keep the telemetry tag examples — tests rely on the label field name.

Tom (Eng-SRE): Quick doc nit on SLA language — current draft uses "best-effort fallback to lower tiers" which product interprets as promise. Suggest: "fallback behavior may be invoked under capacity constraints; customers with reserved pools should pin model versions to avoid fallback". Avoid words like "guaranteed" unless it's backed by the Dedicated SLA table.

Anna (Docs): Good catch. I'll replace "best-effort" with the proposed phrasing and add a sentence pointing to the Reserved SLA table.

deploy-bot: linkcheck started for PR #789

Ravi (Eng-Platform): FYI I ran the local linkcheck; found one broken anchor: /handbook/capacity#fallback-policy (we had used #fallbacks in the new file). I pushed a quick commit to PR to align anchors and update the TOC links. Also fixed an old reference to `tenant_hint` in the API reference.

Anna (Docs): Pushed update: clarified SLA sentence, added migration snippet, fixed anchors per Ravi's commit. Can someone glance at the SDK JS/py examples for idiomatic usage?

Maya (Eng-ML): JS looks fine. For Python, prefer explicit keyword param example so linters and type-checking behave: `client.create_route(model='rdm-large-v1', tenant_label='acct-42', routing={'policy':'cost-first'})`. I'll add that as a tiny patch.

Ravi (Eng-Platform): CI linkcheck now: green. Static build: minor markdown lint warnings (line length), nothing blocking.

deploy-bot: CI: linkcheck ✅, build ✅, markdown-lint warnings: 2

Tom (Eng-SRE): LGTM on SLA wording. One optional ask: add a short example showing how to pin a model in the Dedicated config to avoid fallback during peak windows. That can live under "Operational guidance" rather than the routing examples.

Anna (Docs): Will add a short pinning snippet in a follow-up commit and note it under Operational guidance. For this PR I'll merge after CI completes so the anchor/link fixes go out — follow-up will be a small add. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Maya (Eng-ML): Thanks — will open a small PR with the python snippet and the pinning example if you want me to.

Anna (Docs): Great — please do. Merging now once green.
